messages:
jess: Heads up — CI red on weekly/customer-api image push when publishing build #4523. Noticed after I added a .dockerignore change earlier today. Anyone seen this pattern?

ci-bot: build/4523 failed at push step -> registry.redwood.internal:443
Error: PUT /v2/customer-api/blobs/uploads/... -> 400 Bad Request (chunk mismatch)

mohit: saw similar once when our builder switched from buildkit to kaniko and the layer upload retries ended up with mismatched offsets. Did the runner change?

sam: I didn't change the runner. jess, what did you change in .dockerignore?

jess: Just excluded /tmp and /.cache to shrink image context. Also reordered COPY so build layers changed slightly. I can paste the relevant bits:
```Dockerfile
# before
COPY package.json /app/
RUN npm ci --production
COPY . /app

# after (what I changed)
COPY . /app
COPY package.json /app/
RUN npm ci --production
```

lee: that reorder will invalidate cache for npm install and changes layer sizes. Not ideal. But invalidated cache alone shouldn't give 400 chunk mismatch.

mohit: agree. Two possibilities: 1) registry experienced a multipart upload race and one chunk got corrupted, 2) our builder client retried with different offsets due to a bug (kaniko known issue). Which builder image did this run on?

jess: Runner uses build-node-ubuntu-24 (containerd + kaniko executor). Logs show a few retry lines before the 400.

ci-bot: last logs (snip):
```
W retrying upload chunk: EOF
I upload chunk size=4.2MB offset=8388608
E chunk upload failed: server returned 400 (multipart: unexpected end of part)
```

sam: hmm. Could be transient registry backend flake + cache shift that increased concurrency. Quick triage options: rerun the same job, rerun with --no-cache, or try pushing a locally built image from a dev machine to see if the registry consistently rejects.

jess: I'll rerun with --no-cache first. If it still fails I'll try building locally and pushing. Anyone want me to bisect commits to find when this started?

lee: not necessary yet. Also try adding `REGISTRY_UPLOAD_SINGLE_PART=true` env to force single-part uploads (if supported) to avoid multipart bug. Or bump kaniko to the latest executor image — there was a recent fix.

mohit: good call. Also check registry logs for the upload id to see if the server aborted mid-stream. I'll ssh into registry-prod and grep the logs.

jess: ok kicking off rerun with no-cache now. will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(2m later)

jess: rerun complete — build succeeded locally with --no-cache and push succeeded. CI rerun (same config) also green after second attempt. Looks flaky.

mohit: thanks. I'll correlate registry logs for that upload id and follow up if I see server-side aborts. If we see repeated failures we'll: 1) pin kaniko version in our builders, 2) enable single-part upload flag, and/or 3) revert the Dockerfile reorder until we confirm stability.

sam: please file a short incident note if you find server-side errors. Otherwise we'll treat as transient and keep an eye on pushes for the next 24h.

jess: will do. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
